Confirmation of Candidature (was Thesis Proposal Review before 2024)
Generally, as a PhD student, your major milestone is your Confirmation
of Candidature stage which is around nine months to one year after
your initial enrolment (if full-time). Please take the deadline very
seriously as anyone over 3 months will likely have their scholarship
and enrolment terminated.
Please see all the ANU HDR Policies and Procedures
here.
The primary supervisor can confirm the Chair of the Panel by logging
into
ANUHUB
or if that fails, by emailing our HDR Admin
Team.
Note: We expect you (the HDR student) to organise a 1 on 1 meeting
with the CRP Chair about one month before the Confirmation
submission to give the candidate a chance to discuss any questions
they have about the Confirmation process. However, candidates are
referred to this page and are expected to read it carefully as well as
the documents and pages linked to it, to reduce the CRP Chairâs work.
SOCO CoC Thesis Proposal Requirements
The full proposal should provide evidence of the viability of the
proposed research topic and the capacity of the student to carry out
the proposed research. The full proposal should try to be no longer
than 40 pages (A4, font 12pt) and between 5,000 and 10,000 words. If
there is more work to report than can be fit within these limits,
details should be put into an appendix.
Note: The university has no official page/word limit for the full
proposal; this mandate is from the SOCO HDR Committee.
The full proposal is expected to contain the following elements:
A clear motivation(s) for the proposed research.
The clear goals/objectives/research questions/hypotheses of the
proposed research, including the overall goal and the specific
objectives.
A literature survey of related research. This should make clear the
difference between the proposed work and the existing work.
A description of what the student has done so far related to the
research goals in the provisional registration periods; giving
details of published/accepted papers, if any.
An outline of the project, including a detailed plan for the
goals/objectives to be carried out in the following years
(particularly the next six months) a timeline for the thesis
(including writing), a possible thesis outline, and the proposed
major contributions.
Special facility/materials needed for the thesis (if any).
A list of relevant references.
NB! Please include any relevant publications that you have under
submission or accepted as an appendix to the CoC proposal report.
Once the proposal is ready, you submit the CoC milestone via
ANUHub. Make sure to add your report in there. Although the panel
chair will then have access to the report and could share it with the
other panel members, it would be helpful for the CoC chair (and speed
up the process) if instead you share the report with
everybody. Nevertheless, make sure to first submit it via ANUHub
first, anyway. Also note that once you submitted, you should schedule
a meeting, check below for details.
SOCO CoC Meeting Procedure
Please note that the Confirmation of Candidature process involves both
a report and a presentation followed by the meeting of the entire
panel that you will chair.
Note: We expect you (the HDR student) to organise a room and a
time for a 2-hour slot with the oral presentation taking place in
the first hour and the meeting of the panel happening right
after. This presentation has to occur 10 working days (i.e., at least
two weeks) or more after the milestone was submitted (cf. p.4,
top-right of CoC
Requirements),
to give the panel members enough time to read it carefully and provide
insightful feedback.
To book a room, please email our administration staff and ask for
help: admin.comp@anu.edu.au. Please
submit the eForms before that meeting and upload your thesis proposal
document as part of it. Submit it early in advance so that the panel
and CoC chair has enough time to read the document before the meeting.
Finally, ensure you complete the relevant CoC eForm that will then go
to the CoC Chair so that they can complete it for the required outcome
to be processed.
CoC Presentation (Public Attendance)
The conduct of the seminar is roughly as follows (the seminars are
generally open to the public or other staff and should be advertised
at least to the relevant cluster):
The primary supervisor introduces the student and their background
and points out the panel members present to ask questions.
The student gives a talk (generally around 40-45 minutes long to
leave time for questions). The student has a right to delay all
questions to the end of the talk if they choose so.
The CoC chair chairs the final Question and Answer session making
sure that the panel members (especially the associate supervisors)
have the opportunity to answer all questions they may have before
the âdecision meetingâ that will follow.
After the panel member questions were exhausted please encourage
audience to ask questions too. Feel free to use the time wisely from
the overall two hour slot.
The CoC Decision Meeting that Follows (Restricted Attendance)
The conduct of the âdecision meetingâ that follows the seminar is
roughly as follows (the student is NOT present at this meeting, only
the panel members and the CoC chair are allowed in this meeting):
To start the meeting, you (the CoC Chair) can choose to briefly
summarise what they thought of the presentation and the written
report (if you choose to read it) as the external chair to the panel
but thatâs about it: the panel examines the PhD confirmation of
candidature while the chair only ensures the fairness of the
process. For example, the CoC Chair is not expected to read the
proposal or judge the quality of work as such but let the panel do
it.
CoC Chair needs to take some notes to support or comment on the
final outcome as decided by the panel and chair the meetings to
ensure this is done fairly and in an ordered fashion.
CoC Chair Can use the ANU CoC Report Template found here in PDF
form format: ANU CoC
SharePoint. The
CoC chair has to fill out this form and upload it as part of the
eForm submission.
Important: Everything the CoC Chair writes in the eForm text
fields and all uploaded documents (including the CoC report) will be
shared with the student. Please phrase your assessment and any
feedback accordingly.
The panel members starting with the most removed (i.e. associate
supervisors) to the closest members (i.e. primary supervisor) then
speak in turn with what their thoughts were on the report and the
presentation and you take notes as the chair.
The primary supervisor will be able to talk at length - all we are
asking here is to let associate supervisors speak first and speak
out loudly what they thought before letting primary supervisor speak
and contribute to avoid confirmation bias.
This way the primary supervisor who knows the work the closest
speaks after the associates - this is very important to ensure that
any external feedback is taken into account as someone too close to
the student may miss things that are sometimes obvious.
Please ask the primary supervisor not to speak at first and delay
any comments until the discussion session. After this everyone can
speak to actually make the decision, only the initial statement has
to be done in order form associates to primary.
Once everyone has spoken in the above turn, you open the discussion
as the chair aiming to arrive at the outcome which can range from
accepting the candidateâs thesis proposal as is to recommending
withdrawal from the program or conversion to Master of Philosophy.

Thesis Examiners Nominations
When it comes to the examination, if you are a current HDR supervisor
at the School of Computing, please note that the following rules are
applied within CSS when it comes to nominating examiners. Please see
the ANU HDR Procedure: Submission and Examination of Theses
here.
We require 3, not just 2 examiners to prevent frequent issues with
non-timely return of the reports or conflicting results. We think
that it is in the students and our best interest to have three.
We can only accept clearly non-conflicted examiners who have
supervised students before and are publishing actively and where
there was no publication with any of the panel members in the last 5
years (or ideally longer). Generally, itâs also better for the
student as they donât need to argue that there was no CoI in the
context of their thesis examination. This excludes but is not
limited to the following:
Joint paper with a student or panel member in the last five years
Joint recipient of a grant with a student or panel member in the
last five years
Supervisor/supervisee relationship ever
Close personal relationship with a student or panel member
Financial or other interest in research results
Employment at an institution involved in research
Finally, please ensure that you checked with the examiners you are
nominating that they are happy to examine the thesis before
nominating them.
